summary: Every eval subject was composed from `config.example.toml` -- a safe template for a FRESH deployment, so it ships with almost everything off. 65 values differed from the deployment, including `llm.model` (`ollamacloud/deepseek-v4-flash:0731` vs `nora`), `llm.reasoning_effort`, and `relevance_gate`, `participation`, `standing`, `culture`, `notes`, `dreamer`, `search`, `online`, `weather`, `route` and `preview` all DISABLED. Every case ever run measured a different model, at a different reasoning effort, with most of Nora switched off. Subjects now compose `config.evaluation.toml`, rebuilt per run from the deployment's own config.
details: No case could have caught it, which is why it survived the whole suite rebuild. `design/evaluation/01-boundaries.md` §5's rule 4 -- 'nothing reaches the model that the deployment would not send' -- constrains the PROMPT, and the prompt was fine. What differed was the reader. Rule 5 is added for the other half: it is the deployment's own model, under its own settings, with its own features on.

`evals/subject_config.py` is the tracked artefact and its OUTPUT is gitignored: the generated config carries the deployment's real values (doctrine canary, room ids, internal endpoints), which is exactly what `.gitignore` keeps `config.toml` untracked for (operator decision 2026-09-07). `python -m evals` rebuilds it before any case via `materialise()`, which REFUSES when the result disagrees with the deployment outside a declared `ALLOWED_TO_DIFFER`, and refuses outright when no deployment config is reachable rather than falling back to the example.

`build()` is pure (text in, text out), so 10 architecture guards hold it against a deployment-SHAPED fixture with no deployment access -- deliberately, because a guard that needed the real config could only SKIP when it was absent, and a skipping guard is the vacuous pass this layer exists to refuse.

Three defects found by writing the guards rather than by reading: (1) `platforms.signal.enabled` was inherited TRUE from the example, so the sandbox would have dialled signal-cli; (2) 'every feature must be on' was the wrong rule -- `notes.curator_enabled`, `notes.discharge_enabled`, `speech.wake.enabled` and `media.describe.audio.enabled` are off in the deployment too, so ON would have been the divergence; (3) a key the deployment SETS but the example never mentions has no line to rewrite and silently took `nora/config.py`'s default -- `store.prune_enabled` defaults True, the deployment sets False, so a sandbox would have PRUNED ITS OWN SEEDED ROWS mid-run.

Corrected by measurement, not argument: an earlier cut forced every platform adapter OFF on the reasoning that evals drive entry points directly and never listen. That produced `StartupError: no platform adapter is enabled` in 22 integration tests, and the reasoning was wrong anyway -- the registry's `self_aliases()` feeds `self_ids`, which `MentionPolicy`/`ReplyToNoraPolicy` match on, and with the text trigger disabled 2026-09-01 mention-and-reply IS the engagement path.

DECLARED DIVERGENCE, not closed: Discord stays disabled in the sandbox because its adapter resolves identity with a live `GET /users/@me` (a placeholder token is HTTP 401, a real one authenticates as the deployment's actual bot). The cost is that Discord mention/reply engagement cannot fire; no corpus exercises it today, and a mention/reply corpus on Discord is blocked on closing this.

WHERE THE SUITE RUNS is now part of the contract (decided 2026-09-21): on the deploy host. With the deployment's features on, composition refuses to start elsewhere -- `[compute]` needs `NORA_DATA_HOST_ROOT`, a HOST-side bind-mount path. `_baseline()` uses `os.environ.setdefault`, which is ONE composition path in two environments rather than two paths: on the deploy host the real credentials win and the tools are production's; elsewhere placeholders fill in and tools degrade to unavailable, which is itself a stated divergence.
